source.note: The source is this repository's own Python implementation, not a second checkout. Cadenza is being rewritten in place (cadenza#8): `src/cadenza/` and `tests/` are the specification until a later PR retires them, so every inventory here is collected from the working tree at the recorded revision.

suite_baseline.reconciliation: `PYTHONPATH=src PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider` at a5672f8 on CPython 3.12.3: 330 passed. No module is skipped at collection time, so collected == the sum of the eight per-file inventories with nothing left over. See parity/source-inventory.manifest.json.

file.note: 11 test functions, 11 collected node ids: nothing in this file is parametrized.

systematic_mappings.why: A direct translation. The default matters: three cases rely on `web` having exactly one alias and `api` having none.
The same helper the compose ledger records, for the same reason. `ProjectNotFoundError` carries no location, so its `message` is the bare text and `match=` and `toMatch` see the same string.
`FieldOrigin` is a frozen object from a factory rather than a frozen dataclass, so equality is structural. `toBe` would be reference equality and would fail on every row.

target_only_tests.why: Every test in this file translates a source case -- but not every one of them comes from `tests/test_resolve.py`. `the digest survives the catalog moving to another file` translates a case of `tests/test_digest.py`, re-pointed here by the pilot that could not port it, and it is claimed by `parity/digest.ledger.json` rather than declared target-only. That is why `scripts/parity-check.mjs` runs its `unmapped` sweep after reading every ledger rather than while reading each one.

inherited_limitations.behaviour: The two not-found cases assert that a suggestion appears and that an unrelated name produces none. Neither pins the ORDER of several suggestions, or the exact cutoff, so a `difflib` port that ranked candidates differently would keep both green.
inherited_limitations.why: The source's own shape. It is not left there: `test/domain/python-semantics.test.ts` asserts the tie-break order, the `n` cap and the 0.6 cutoff against values taken from CPython, and it is declared target-only in `parity/target-only.json` rather than smuggled into this file, because those are claims about `difflib` and not about `tests/test_resolve.py`.

inherited_limitations.behaviour: The suggestion text is the one thing in this belt whose byte-identity with CPython is NOT checked by the differential oracle.
inherited_limitations.why: Deliberate, and agreed with the 窓口 when the second oracle face was approved: the oracle's subject is the PERSISTED value, `resolve_project(...).config_digest`. A refusal message is displayed and never recorded, so a divergence in it costs a confusing sentence rather than a suspect digest -- and a vector of message strings would be a large committed artefact defending the smaller risk.

entries.reason: Same assertion: the snapshot carries the identity, the source and the base branch.

entries.target_id: test/application/resolve.test.ts::resolve_project > resolves by alias to the same immutable identity
entries.reason: Same assertion: an alias is a way in, not a different project, so the two snapshots are equal. Adapted because the source compares two frozen dataclasses with `==` and `ResolvedProject` here is a frozen object, so the comparison is `toEqual` (structural) rather than `toBe` (`Object.is`, which would compare two distinct objects by reference and always fail).

entries.target_id: test/application/resolve.test.ts::resolve_project > aliases travel with the snapshot as information
entries.reason: Same assertion: the aliases travel in DECLARED order, not sorted -- the sort happens inside the digest payload and nowhere else.

entries.target_id: test/application/resolve.test.ts::resolve_project > the snapshot carries the config digest
entries.reason: Same assertion, both halves: the snapshot's digest is the one `configDigest` computes for the composed project, and it carries the `sha256:` prefix.
Same assertion: the overriding layer owns the field it stated and the earlier layer keeps the rest.

entries.target_id: test/application/resolve.test.ts::resolve_project > an unknown name is refused with the closest candidates
entries.reason: Same assertion: a near miss is named. It is only the same assertion because `difflib.get_close_matches` was PORTED rather than approximated -- `SequenceMatcher.ratio` is not edit distance, and a substitute measure would suggest a different set. See `src/domain/python-difflib.ts` and the target-only cases in `test/domain/python-semantics.test.ts`.

entries.target_id: test/application/resolve.test.ts::resolve_project > an unrelated name is refused without inventing a candidate
entries.reason: Same assertion: below the 0.6 cutoff nothing is suggested, and the message does not carry the suggestion preamble at all.

entries.target_id: test/application/resolve.test.ts::resolve_project > a tombstoned project no longer resolves
entries.reason: Same assertion: removal in composition is removal from the namespace.

entries.target_id: test/application/resolve.test.ts::resolve_project > not found is not a catalog error
entries.reason: Same assertion about the same class relationship. Adapted because `issubclass` has no expression in TypeScript -- a class is a value and a type, and only the value carries a prototype chain -- so the question is asked of an instance with `instanceof`, which walks exactly what `issubclass` walks. It is also the form a caller would actually use to tell "your catalog is broken" from "no such project", which is what the case is about.

entries.target_id: test/application/resolve.test.ts::resolve_project > provenance is total over every field of the snapshot
entries.reason: Same assertion, and the same three parts: the aliases default to empty, provenance covers all four fields, and the default's origin names the layer that made it. `set(resolved.provenance)` over a mapping's keys becomes `new Set(Object.keys(...))`.

entries.target_id: test/application/resolve.test.ts::resolve_project > a later layer stating aliases owns their provenance
entries.reason: Same assertion: stating `aliases` in a later layer moves their provenance and leaves the rest alone. Resolving by the NEW alias is part of the case and is kept.
